title: Simplicial presheaf presentation of one-sided fibrations
statement:
Use simplicial sets, Kan complexes, weak homotopy equivalences, internal functor simplicial sets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], one-sided fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and the coherent realization $\mathfrak C$ and simplicial-category terminology of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. For a simplicial set $K$, its opposite has $(K^{\mathrm{op}})_n=K_n$ with faces $d_i^{\mathrm{op}}=d_{n-i}$ and degeneracies $s_i^{\mathrm{op}}=s_{n-i}$ in degree $n$; the opposite simplicial category has $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}(x,y)=\mathcal C(y,x)$ with reversed composition. Fix a universe $\mathcal V$ and a $\mathcal V$-small simplicial set $S$. The enriched category $\mathsf D_S$ consists of simplicial functors $\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V}$. It has a simplicial projective model structure with objectwise weak homotopy equivalences and objectwise Kan fibrations; cofibrations have the left lifting property against the objectwise trivial Kan fibrations. Cofibrant and fibrant have the meanings of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Its mapping complex has $n$-simplices the enriched natural maps $F\times\Delta^n\to G$. Let $\mathsf D_S^{cf}$ be its full simplicial subcategory of cofibrant-fibrant objects. Let $\mathsf{RFib}(S)$ be the simplicial category of right fibrations over $S$, with mapping complex $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(X,Y)$ consisting in degree $n$ of maps $X\times\Delta^n\to Y$ over $S$.

The cone functor $T:(\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V})_{/S}\to\mathsf D_S$, $p\mapsto T_p$, has an ordinary right adjoint $U_S$. There is a simplicial structure on this unstraightening functor $U_S$ whose restriction $\mathsf D_S^{cf}\to\mathsf{RFib}(S)$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Its underlying simplicial set is specified as follows. For $p:X\to S$, put $M_p=\mathfrak C[X\star\Delta^0]\amalg_{\mathfrak C[X]}\mathfrak C[S]$, write $v$ for the new cone vertex, and put $T_p(s)=M_p(s,v)$, contravariantly in $s$ by precomposition. The simplices of $U_SF$ over $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S$ are the enriched natural maps $T_\sigma\to F$; operators are induced by simplex operators. The join here has $(X\star Y)_r=X_r\amalg Y_r\amalg\coprod_{a+b+1=r}X_a\times Y_b$, with ordered concatenation operators, and the pushout is the categorical colimit of simplicial categories.

For every objectwise Kan $F$, $(U_SF)_s$ is naturally weakly equivalent to $F(s)$. The functor $U_S$ carries objectwise weak equivalences between such diagrams to equivalences of right fibrations. For every map $u:B\to S$, there is a natural isomorphism $u^*U_SF\cong U_B(F\circ\mathfrak C[u]^{\mathrm{op}})$, compatible with composition of base maps. For a constant diagram with Kan value $X$, there is a natural map $S\times X\to U_S(\mathrm{const}\,X)$ which is a weak homotopy equivalence on every vertex fiber. The constructions stay in $\mathcal V$.

For any $Z\to S$ and right fibration $Y\to S$, $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(Z,Y)$ is Kan. A map between right fibrations over $S$ is an equivalence in $\mathsf{RFib}(S)$ if and only if its maps on vertex fibers are weak homotopy equivalences. Here equivalence means a simplicial map with an inverse up to simplicial homotopies over $S$. The category $(\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V})_{/S}$ has a simplicial contravariant model structure: cofibrations are monomorphisms, weak equivalences are the maps $X\to Y$ for which $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(Y,Z)\to\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(X,Z)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every right fibration $Z\to S$, and fibrations are characterized by lifting against the trivial cofibrations. Its fibrant objects are exactly the right fibrations, and every object is cofibrant. The adjunction $T\dashv U_S$ is a Quillen equivalence. Here Quillen equivalence means that the left adjoint preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations and, for cofibrant $X$ and fibrant $F$, $TX\to F$ is a weak equivalence if and only if its adjoint $X\to U_SF$ is a weak equivalence. Tensor and enriched mapping objects in the slice are $X\times K\to S$ and $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}$.

The covariant model structure on $(\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V})_{/S}$ is obtained from the contravariant one over $S^{\mathrm{op}}$ by the ordinary equivalence $X\mapsto X^{\mathrm{op}}$. It is also simplicial for the same tensor and mapping objects, all objects are cofibrant, and its fibrant objects are exactly the left fibrations. Weak equivalences between left fibrations are exactly the maps which are weak homotopy equivalences on vertex fibers. Put $\mathsf D^{\mathrm{cov}}_S=\operatorname{Fun}_{\Delta}(\mathfrak C[S],\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V})$ with its simplicial projective model structure. Reversal of ordered vertex labels gives $\mathfrak C[S^{\mathrm{op}}]\cong\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}$. Define $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_S F=(U_{S^{\mathrm{op}}}F)^{\mathrm{op}}$: here $F:\mathfrak C[S]\to\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V}$ is regarded, after taking opposites, as a contravariant diagram on $S^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the opposite of the resulting right fibration is a left fibration over $S$. As an ordinary functor $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_S$ is the right adjoint in a Quillen equivalence from the covariant model structure to $\mathsf D^{\mathrm{cov}}_S$. Its infinity functor is its right-derived functor, obtained by localizing its restriction to objectwise Kan diagrams. Its fiber at $s$ is $(U_{S^{\mathrm{op}}}F)_s^{\mathrm{op}}$, naturally equivalent as a space to $F(s)$. It preserves objectwise weak equivalences between these diagrams, and its base-change isomorphisms and size assertions are obtained by applying opposites to those for $U$. The opposite of the constant-product map is $S\times X^{\mathrm{op}}\to U^{\mathrm{cov}}_S(\mathrm{const}\,X)$ and is a weak homotopy equivalence on vertex fibers. For any $Z\to S$ and left fibration $Y\to S$, $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(Z,Y)$ is Kan; a map between left fibrations is a simplicial homotopy equivalence over $S$ if and only if it is a weak homotopy equivalence on vertex fibers.

source.place: Section 2.2.1 (cone construction); Proposition 2.2.1.1 (base change); Proposition 2.2.3.11 (printed p.83, enriched presentation); Lemmas 2.2.3.4 and 2.2.3.6 (Kan mapping complexes and fiberwise equivalences); Remark 2.2.2.11 and Proposition 2.2.2.9 (vertex fibers and constant-product map). Projective model structure: Proposition A.3.3.2. Covariant assertions are the opposite-simplicial-set dual. Read online; archival HTT WANTED. No Stacks tag. Model structures and Quillen equivalence: Propositions 2.1.4.7–8, Remark 2.1.4.12, Theorem 2.2.1.2, Corollaries 2.2.3.12–13; covariant adjunction is the ordinary opposite-base dual, without an assertion that the opposite operation preserves simplicial enrichment.

proof.text: The Kan model category of simplicial sets is combinatorial and simplicial by [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model]. Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] to the small simplicial category $\mathfrak C[S]^{op}$. This gives precisely the asserted projective model structure on $\mathsf D_S$, with objectwise tensor and cotensor. Its enriched end imposes the action-square equations, so its $n$-simplices are enriched natural maps $F\times\Delta^n\to G$. No local Kan assumption on $\mathfrak C[S]$ is needed.

source.place: Proposition A.3.3.2, enriched projective model structure

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model] for the ordinary contravariant model on $\mathrm{sSet}_{/S}$. Every object is cofibrant since $\varnothing\to X$ is monic, and the fibrant objects are exactly right fibrations. In [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen] take $D=\mathfrak C[S]^{op}$ and $\phi$ the identity of $\mathfrak C[S]$. Its cone $M_{a,\phi}$ is exactly $M_p$ in the statement. Hence its left adjoint is the specified $T$, its right adjoint has exactly the displayed simplex formula for $U_S$, and its ordinary adjunction is a Quillen equivalence. In particular $U_SF$ is a right fibration for every objectwise Kan $F$. This step uses the ordinary, more general straightening theorem, with no claim yet about simplicial enrichment.

For any $X\to S$, $X\times\Delta^\bullet$ with projection augmentation is a cosimplicial frame in that ordinary slice model. Indeed its latching map is $X\times\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow X\times\Delta^n$, a monomorphism: taking a product preserves the colimit of the face inclusions degreewise. The last-vertex inclusion $\{n\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ is right anodyne. To see this, start from vertex $n$ and, for each nonempty $\tau\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ in increasing cardinality $r$, attach the simplex on $\tau\cup\{n\}$ along its last horn $\Lambda_r^r$; the new cells are exactly $\tau$ and $\tau\cup\{n\}$. Every other face has already been attached. The product theorem [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product], applied with $\varnothing\hookrightarrow X$, makes $X\times\{n\}\to X\times\Delta^n$ right anodyne and hence a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model]. The projection back to $X$ is therefore a weak equivalence by two-out-of-three. Degree zero is the identity. Apply [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping]: for every right fibration $Y$, $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(X,Y)$ is Kan and represents the localized mapping space, naturally in the two inputs.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.3.4 and its right-anodyne prism argument; cosimplicial-frame version of Remark A.3.1.8

proof.text: A slice weak equivalence $f:A\to B$ induces weak equivalences $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(B,Y)\to\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(A,Y)$ for all right fibrations $Y$, since the frame comparison in step 3 identifies these with localized mapping spaces. Conversely suppose all these mapping maps are weak equivalences. Every localized object is equivalent to a fibrant one by [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping], so on components precomposition by $qf$ is bijective into every object. This forces $qf$ invertible: surjectivity with target $qA$ gives $g:qB\to qA$ with $gqf=1$, and injectivity with target $qB$ gives $(qf)g=1$ after precomposing with $qf$. The homotopy category of the coherent localization is the ordinary localization: its universal property for ordinary targets is obtained by taking components of the coherent universal property. Thus [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] implies that $f$ is a model weak equivalence. This proves precisely the mapping-test definition of weak equivalence in the item.

source.place: Contravariant model equivalences; ordinary localization detection and frame comparison

proof.text: Let $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ be any slice monomorphism and $Y\to S$ a right fibration. The restriction $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(B,Y)\to\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(A,Y)$ is a right fibration: a lifting square against a right horn transposes to a lifting square for $Y\to S$ against the pushout product of that horn with $i$, which is right anodyne by [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product]. Lifting against the entire right-anodyne class follows from lifting against its generators by taking pushouts, successive compatible lifts, and retracts. The base of this restriction is Kan by step 3. Therefore [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber] makes the restriction a Kan fibration. If $i$ is also a slice weak equivalence, step 4 says this Kan fibration is a weak homotopy equivalence, hence trivial.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.3.4; right fibration over a Kan complex is a Kan fibration

proof.text: The slice is enriched by $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}$ and tensored by $X\otimes K=X\times K\to S$. A cotensor is $S\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,S)}\operatorname{Fun}(K,X)$, using the constant-map inclusion of $S$; the tensor/cotensor adjunction follows by transposing maps $Z\times K\to X$ over $S$. For a slice monomorphism $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ and a simplicial monomorphism $j:K\hookrightarrow L$, the pushout product has domain $(A\times L)\cup(B\times K)$, so is monic. Mapping it into a right fibration $Y$ is exactly the mapping-space map obtained from $j$ and the restriction fibration of step 5. The Cartesian Kan-model SM7 axiom supplied by [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model] makes this a trivial Kan fibration if either $i$ is a slice weak equivalence (step 5) or $j$ is a Kan weak equivalence. Step 4 then makes the pushout product a slice weak equivalence. By the tensor/mapping adjunction, this pushout-product condition is the mapping-space SM7 condition: a lifting square for the latter transposes to one for the former, and model lifting against (trivial) cofibrations gives the required (trivial) Kan fibrations. This proves the asserted simplicial model structure, with the unchanged ordinary weak equivalences and fibrations.

source.place: Cartesian simplicial structure; Lemma 2.2.3.4 and SM7 via pushout products

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] to the simplicial slice model of step 6. Since all objects are cofibrant, its bifibrant simplicial category is exactly $\mathsf{RFib}(S)$, and its mapping spaces are the actual displayed functor complexes. A weak equivalence between right fibrations becomes invertible in the localization, so its inverse is represented by a vertex in the corresponding Kan mapping complex; its two identity equations on components give simplicial homotopies to the identities. In a Kan complex a finite zigzag of edges can be replaced by a single edge using horn fillers (reverse an edge by a 2-horn and compose edges by a 2-horn), so these are homotopies with parameter $\Delta^1$. Conversely such an inverse makes the localized arrow invertible, and [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] reflects this. Finally [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model] identifies these weak equivalences between right fibrations with the weak homotopy equivalences on every strict vertex fiber.

Put $V(K)=|K|_Q$ and $R_Q(T)=\operatorname{Sing}_Q T$ as in [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution]. The cosimplicial $Q$ is a frame on the point in the Kan model: [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching] gives $Q^0=\Delta^0$, monic latching maps and weak contractibility of each degree, and hence the frame augmentation to the point. Thus [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping] makes $R_Q(T)$ Kan for Kan $T$. The cosimplicial map $p^n:Q^n\to\Delta^n$ defines a natural simplicial map $\eta_T:T\to R_Q(T)$ by $x\mapsto x p^n$. For Kan $T$, evaluation gives $e_T V(\eta_T)=p_T$. Both $e_T$ and $p_T$ are weak equivalences by [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution], so $V(\eta_T)$ is a weak equivalence. Naturality $p_{R_QT}V(\eta_T)=\eta_Tp_T$ and the same theorem then imply that $\eta_T$ is a weak equivalence. Its formula preserves terminal objects and products exactly, since maps into a product are pairs of maps.

Apply [lem-coef-unstraightening-external-products] with $\phi=1$ to obtain $U_S(F\times K)\cong U_SF\times R_QK$. An $n$-simplex $h:F\times\Delta^n\to G$ now induces the composite
$$U_SF\times\Delta^n\xrightarrow{1\times\eta_{\Delta^n}}U_SF\times R_Q\Delta^n\cong U_S(F\times\Delta^n)\xrightarrow{U_Sh}U_SG.$$
Naturality of $\eta$ makes these commute with every simplex operator. The unit identification and $Q^0=\Delta^0$ show that vertices recover the given ordinary functor. The associativity compatibility of the external-product isomorphism and the product compatibility of $\eta$ show that enriched composition is preserved: both composites for $F\times K\to G$, $G\times L\to H$ are obtained by applying $U_S$ to $F\times K\times L\to H$ and precomposing with $1\times\eta_K\times\eta_L$. Terminal compatibility gives identities. This constructs the asserted simplicial structure. Apply [lem-coef-enriched-right-quillen-equivalence] to $T\dashv U_S$: steps 1 and 6 give the two simplicial model categories, every slice object is cofibrant, and step 2 gives the ordinary Quillen equivalence. Its conclusion is exactly the Dwyer--Kan equivalence $\mathsf D_S^{cf}\to\mathsf{RFib}(S)$.

source.place: Remark 2.2.2.12; Remark A.3.1.9 and Proposition A.3.1.10

proof.text: The precise fiber formula in [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen] is $(U_SF)_s\cong R_QF(s)$. For objectwise Kan $F$, the map $\eta$ of step 8 gives the claimed natural weak equivalence from $F(s)$ to that fiber. If $F\to G$ is an objectwise weak equivalence between objectwise Kan diagrams, its commutative squares with these $\eta$ maps make every map on $U$-fibers a weak equivalence by two-out-of-three. Step 7 gives the asserted equivalence of right fibrations. For a constant diagram, [lem-coef-unstraightening-external-products] gives $U_S(\mathrm{const}\,X)\cong U_S(*)\times R_QX$. The simplex formula gives $U_S(*)=S$: there is exactly one natural map from any $T_\sigma$ to the terminal diagram. Consequently $1_S\times\eta_X$ is the required natural constant-product map, and is a weak equivalence on every fiber when $X$ is Kan.

Let $u:B\to S$ and let $\beta:\Delta^n\to B$. The cone defining $T_{u\beta}$ is obtained from the cone for $T_\beta$ by extending the base $\mathfrak C[B]\to\mathfrak C[S]$. A natural map from its new-vertex mapping diagram to $F$ amounts to its values on the cone generators, with the action equations for $\mathfrak C[S]$; these are exactly a map from the cone diagram over $B$ to $F\circ\mathfrak C[u]^{op}$. More explicitly such a map is a simplicial functor from the cone pushout to the simplicial category obtained by adjoining a vertex $v$ to $\mathfrak C[S]$ with maps $s\to v$ given by $F(s)$, maps out of $v$ empty except its identity, and composition given by the $F$-action, fixing the base and $v$. The pushout universal property identifies these functors with the corresponding functors over $\mathfrak C[B]$. This uses exactly the cone pushout formula of [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen]. The bijection commutes with simplex restriction, giving the claimed base-change isomorphism. For two base maps both bijections are the same restriction of cone generators, proving compatibility with composition and identities. Finally all joins, degreewise maps, enriched colimits and natural-transformation sets here are indexed by $\mathcal V$-small sets. Pushouts of small enriched categories can be built from finite strings of morphisms modulo the composition relations, still in $\mathcal V$. Therefore $T$, each $U_SF$, their products, fibers and base changes stay in $\mathcal V$. This does not assert that the set of all $\mathcal V$-small diagrams itself belongs to $\mathcal V$.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.1.1, base change, with cone pushout universal property and size bookkeeping

proof.text: Opposites are involutive ordinary equivalences of simplicial-set slices. Reversing vertex labels identifies the subset posets defining $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$ in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], with source and target exchanged. It preserves inclusion and union, and commutes with simplex maps after the reversal $\alpha\mapsto r\alpha r$; extension over the simplex colimits gives $\mathfrak C[S^{op}]\cong\mathfrak C[S]^{op}$ naturally. Opposites take the $i$th horn to the $(n-i)$th horn and therefore take right fibrations to left fibrations. They preserve monomorphisms. Ordinary geometric realization of $K^{op}$ is naturally homeomorphic to that of $K$: on a simplex send barycentric coordinates $(t_0,\ldots,t_n)$ to $(t_n,\ldots,t_0)$ in the same underlying simplex of $K$; the reversed face and degeneracy formulas give exactly the gluing identities. Thus opposites preserve Kan complexes and weak homotopy equivalences. Transport the ordinary contravariant model and the ordinary Quillen equivalence of step 2 over $S^{op}$ through this ordinary equivalence. The resulting fibrant objects and fiber criterion are the asserted ones. It is also simplicial with the stated tensor: the opposite of a pushout product is the pushout product of the two opposites; monomorphisms and Kan weak equivalences in the parameter are preserved, so step 6 proves its SM7 axiom. One need not make opposite into a simplicial functor for this argument. Moreover $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(Z,Y)^{op}\cong\operatorname{Fun}_{/S^{op}}(Z^{op},Y^{op})$ by reversing the parameter simplex. Step 3 and preservation of Kan complexes give the left-fibration mapping assertion; step 7 and this identification give its simplicial homotopy-equivalence criterion.

source.place: Remark 2.1.4.12, opposite duality; Section 1.1.5 subset-poset construction

proof.text: After the preceding coherent-realization identification the projective diagram category over $S^{op}$ is exactly $\mathsf D^{cov}_S$, with the same values and projective weak equivalences. The transported ordinary right adjoint is therefore exactly $U^{cov}_SF=(U_{S^{op}}F)^{op}$. Apply [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] to the transported Quillen adjunction: its right-derived infinity functor is computed on projectively fibrant, namely objectwise Kan, diagrams. Its restriction to those diagrams preserves all weak equivalences and its localization computes the right-derived functor, since fibrant replacement is naturally weakly equivalent to the identity. Its vertex fiber is $(R_QF(s))^{op}$; step 8 and the realization-coordinate reversal in step 12 identify this naturally as a space with $F(s)$. This identification is an equivalence in spaces, not an asserted natural simplicial map from $K^{op}$ to $K$. Applying opposites to steps 10–11 gives preservation of objectwise weak equivalences, base change, size and the map $S\times X^{op}\to U^{cov}_S(\mathrm{const}\,X)$ with the claimed fiber property. Thus every covariant clause follows from the stated ordinary transport, without assuming that the original cone left adjoint is simplicially enriched.

source.place: Remark 2.1.4.12 and ordinary derived adjunction applied to the opposite-base presentation

proof_origin.place: Section 2.2 and Appendix A.3.1; expansion using the existing general unmarked Quillen theorem, frame arguments and opposite transport. HTT read online; archival copy WANTED.
